 City of La Verne, Development Review Committee
Agenda Report
DATE:  September 5, 2023

TO:  Development Review Committee

FROM:  Gabriel Rivera, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT:  CASE NUMBER 79-23VAR, 83-23PPR, and 84-23CUP – 1020
  BASELINE ROAD – VARIANCE TO DECREASE FRONT SETBACK
  AND AMENDMENT TO 125-14CUP FOR THE ADDITION OF TWO
  CARPORTS.

SUMMARY
The applicant, Milad Queijan, on behalf of the Antiochian House of Studies, has submitted
an application for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) amending the original Master Plan for
the site to allow the proposed carports to be constructed and another application for a
Variance to decrease the front yard setback to 9 feet 4 inches, in order to construct two
carports at 1020 Baseline Road.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the Development Review Committee forward a recommendation
to the Planning Commission to approve Case No. 79-23VAR and Case No. 84-23CUP
based on this staff report. Staff also recommends the Development Review Committee
approve Case No. 83-23PPR based on this staff report and the draft conditions of
approval.

BACKGROUND
The property at 1020 Baseline Road originally had a single-family home, which was
referred to as the Hormel House. The Hormel House was originally constructed in the
1930s and operated as a citrus ranch, which was accessed by Foothill Boulevard. When
the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan (FBSP) was adopted back in July of 1989, the house
became a non-conforming residential use since the site was designated as a commercial
zone within the FBSP. The Hormel House was later purchased by the Antiochian
Orthodox Christian Archdiocese of North America.

The Antiochian Institute is a non-profit organization of the Antiochian Orthodox Christian
Archdiocese of North America, which is a province of a nearly 2000-year-old apostolic
Christian Church of Antioch. The church now includes over 275 churches throughout the
United States and Canada. The Institute itself focuses on pursing theological research to
educate their clergy, publish authorized texts, and serve as a point of reference between
the Archdiocese and all other churches/organizations.

DISCUSSION
In October of 2014, an Antiochian Institute was proposed by the Antiochian Institute
Archdiocese at 1020 Baseline Road. The proposal required a zone change from the
FBSP to the Institutional zone, a General Plan Amendment to Community Facility, along
 Case No. 79-23VAR, 83-23PPR, 84-23CUP – 1020 Baseline Road
September 5, 2023
Page 2

with a Master Plan for the property. The proposal was approved by the City Council, under
Resolution No. 15-08 and Ordinance No. 1051, on March 2, 2015.

The original Master Plan, under Resolution No. 1146 (125-14CUP), required that
improvements to the site be completed in 2 phases. Phase 1 of the project involved
allowing the Hormel House to be used as the Antiochian Institute, along with minor interior
remodeling, a new 10 space parking lot, and connecting the property to the public sewer
system. Phase 1 of the Master Plan was completed, with the exception of the parking lot.
In 2022, the applicant then moved forward with proposing Phase 2 of the project, which
involved the construction of a multi-purpose hall, semi-subterranean study room, and the
parking lot outlined from Phase 1 of the project. On June 13, 2022, the Planning
Commission approved, under Resolution No. 1287 and No. 1288 (Case No. 46-22CUP,
17-22VAR), the aforementioned Phase 2 proposal.

Prior to the applicant submitting for plan check for Phase 2, the applicant had discovered
that the required solar panel system, which would be located on the roof of the multi-
purpose room, would not be in optimal location to receive sunlight. Therefore, the
applicant is proposing two carports (Section A and Section B) within the approved Phase
2 parking lot, which would then house the solar panels on the roofs of the carport.

The Master Plan for the site requires that a Conditional Use Permit be obtained to amend
the original Master Plan, which would allow for any new developments of new buildings
on the site. The applicant is proposing a Master Plan amendment through a Conditional
Use Permit for the 2 new proposed carports in order to satisfy this requirement.

SITE PLAN REVIEW
The applicant is requesting to also obtain a Variance for a 9-foot 4-inch front yard setback
to allow for the construction of the carports. The applicants are seeking the variance due
to there being no other optimal space to place the solar panel system other than the
Phase 2 parking lot. In order to accommodate this, 2 carports were proposed which would
feature the solar panel system on the roof. Due to the Phase 2 parking lot layout, the
optimal spot for the solar panels would be on the north side of the parking lot area. The
north parking spaces of the lot are within the front yard setback area. The property is
located within the Institutional zone, which requires a minimum front yard setback of 25
feet or the height of the building, whichever is greater. If the proposed Variance were to
be approved, the carports would be infringing 15 feet 8 inches into the front yard setback.
Therefore, the two proposed carports would be infringing in the front yard setback area.
The proposed carports, designated as Section A and Section B on the plans (Attachment
4), will be located at the north side of the Phase 2 parking lot, adjacent to Baseline Road.
Section A will be 100 feet 5 inches by 19 feet 2 inches and will approximately cover
1,924.65 square feet of the parking lot. Section B will be 85 feet 6 inches by 20 feet 2
inches and will approximately cover 1,724.25 Square feet of the parking lot. The original
approved parking lot, under Phase 2, was approved for 39 spaces. With this current
proposal, there would be no spaces lost. The proposed carports will also feature the solar
panel system on the roofs. Section A will feature 77 solar panels, while Section B will
feature 67 panels. The driveway entrance to the phase 2 parking lot will have a 26-foot
 Case No. 79-23VAR, 83-23PPR, 84-23CUP – 1020 Baseline Road
September 5, 2023
Page 3

wide 6 foot tall gate that is connected between both carports as shown on Attachment 4.
The applicants are also proposing a 6-foot-high CMU block wall that would enclose the
parking lot, proposed carports, the existing building, and Phase 2 buildings as shown on
Attachment 4.
The Police Department has reviewed the proposal and is in support of the project. They
have added a condition of approval which states that if there are frequent calls of service
to the site, then a fence would be required at the front of the property adjacent to Baseline
Road for further security. An additional condition has been added to close the spaces at
the middle of the proposed carports as shown on Attachment 4. The Fire Department has
also reviewed the proposal, requiring a Knox box for the driveway gate.
ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW The Master Plan for the site requires that any new
construction be in line with the original architectural style of the existing historic structure
(Hormel House). The proposed carports are in line with the architectural style of the
existing historic structure. The exterior elevations of the carports, which are visible from
Baseline Road, feature arches which are 7 feet 3 inches tall by 8 feet 11 inches wide and
will be screened by a lattice cover. The lattice cover will then feature vegetation as shown
by Attachment 4. Both carports will have a max height of 13 feet 1 inches. The applicants
are also proposing a wall sign to Section A which will have a natural rust color and LED
lighting as shown on Attachment 4. The La Verne Municipal Code permits wall signs in
Institutional zones per Section 17.20.020. Staff recommends the Development Review
Committee have the sign be brought back to the Development Review Committee for
review under a separate precise plan review submittal.

COMPATIBILITY WITH SURROUNDING USES
This site is within the institutional zone with single-family residential properties to the
north, a community facility to the east, commercial to the west, and the 210 Freeway to
the south. The carports will be compatible with the surrounding uses.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
A Mitigated Negative Declaration was prepared for the site n 2014, under Case No. 125-
14CUP, in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the La
Verne Environmental Guidelines. It was found that there would be no significant
environmental impacts resulting from the project proposal after mitigation measures were
taken. This project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
per Section 15303(e) and the La Verne Environmental Guidelines. No further
environmental review is required.

SUBJECT:  CASE NO. 83-23PPR - CONDITIONAL APPROVAL
  1020 BASELINE ROAD – A REQUEST TO CONSTRUCT TWO
  CARPORTS FOR SOLAR PANELS.

Dear Mr. Queijan:

The Community Development Department has considered your application to
construct two carports within the front yard setback for solar panels at 1020
Baseline Road. In accordance with chapter 18.16 of the La Verne Municipal Code,
your project has been approved based upon the following findings:

1.  The subject application is consistent with the general plan and
  conforms to all specific plans, zoning, and other applicable
  ordinances and subdivision requirements and resolutions.

  The construction of the proposed buildings require approval of a variance
  (Case No. 79-23VAR) since it will be located within the required front yard
  setback of the Institutional zone. The proposed buildings meet all other
  standards of the La Verne Municipal Code and the Institutional zone.

2.  The site is safe, functional and environmentally sensitive to the
  surroundings. Grading, where required, minimizes environmental
  damage to the extent possible.

  The site will remain safe and functional after the project is completed. The
  proposed buildings will not have a substantive effect on site safety and
  function of the site.

3.  The architecture proposed observes community standards and
  protects the character of the adjacent development.

  The proposed buildings are similar to the style to the other structure located
  on the site. The proposed buildings will match the architectural
  characteristics and use materials that match the existing structure on site.

4.  The landscaping plan ensures visual relief, providing an attractive
  environment for the public’s enjoyment.
 83-23PPR 1020 Baseline Road
September 13, 2023
Page 2

  Landscape changes are not proposed with this application.

Approval of Case No. 83-23PPR is subject to the following conditions:

  1.  The applicant shall abide by the attached Standard List of
  Conditions.

  2.  Final approval of Case No. 83-23PPR is contingent on the approval of
  Case No. 79-23VAR and Case No. 84-23CUP.

  3.  The colors and materials to be used shall be in accordance with the
  approved colors and materials submitted by the applicant and on file
  with the Community Development Department.

  4.  Any revisions to the approved plans shall require review and approval
  by the Community Development Department.

  5.  If there are frequent calls for Police Department services at the site, a
  fence shall be required in front of the carport.

  6.  Approval of the precise plan application is conditional upon privileges
  being used within one year of the effective approval date.

  7.  No temporary buildings other than construction offices shall be
  permitted on the site.

  8.  Applicant shall revise plans to enclose areas called out on the site plan.

  9.  The applicant shall comply with all National Pollutant Discharge
  Elimination System requirements.

  10.  All requirements of the Public Works Department shall be met prior to
  issuance of building permits. Work in or adjacent to the public right of
  way shall require a public works permit.

  11.  Parking lot lighting and lighting of the buildings shall be reviewed jointly
  by the Police Department and Community Development Department.
  Additional lighting appropriate to the architecture and parking lot shall
  be installed as needed. Field adjustment shall be made to assure that
  light is not spilling into adjacent properties.

  12.  A Knox box shall be installed at the driveway gate.

  13.  The applicant shall submit a new sign plan for the carport to be

  14.  All requirements of the City Engineer shall be met prior to issuance of
